case_name: Union of India and Another v Pushpa Rani and Others
facts: Respondents Pushpa Rani and six others joined service as Clerks in Ambala and Ferozepur Divisions of the Northern Railway.
They were promoted as Senior Clerks and then as Head Clerks.

They filed applications u/s.19 of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985 for quashing the instructions issued by the Railway Board vide letter No.PC-III/2003/CRC/6 dated 9.10.2003 for giving effect to the policy of reservation of posts for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes at the stage of restructuring of Group C and D cadres.

They pleaded that the exercise of restructuring undertaken by the government resulted in upgradation of the existing posts and in view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court, the policy of reservation cannot be applied while making appointment against the upgraded posts.
issues: Whether the policy of reservation of posts for Scheduled Castes/ Scheduled Tribes can be applied at the stage of giving effect to cadre restructuring exercise undertaken pursuant to letter No.PC-III/2003/CRC/6 dated 9.10.2003 issued by the Railway Board
petitioner_arguments: The policy of reservation was rightly made applicable in relation to the additional posts.

Restructuring of cadres undertaken for enhancing organizational efficiency and functional, operational and administrative requirements cannot be treated as a simple exercise for upgradation of existing posts
The Railway Board did not commit illegality by issuing direction for implementation of the policy of reservation qua those posts
respondent_arguments: The directions given by the Tribunal are liable to be set aside because its interpretation of the policy of restructuring is also contrary to the law laid down by the Constitution Bench
Restructuring of Group C and D cadres is nothing but an exercise for upgradation of the existing posts

If the policy of reservation is applied at the stage of restructuring of Group C and D cadres then the same would amount to giving double benefit to the members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, who had already been given out-of turn promotions
court_reasoning: The Railway Establishment Code (hereinafter referred to as 'the Code') was first published in September 1940.
Paragraphs 103(7), 119, 120, 123 and 124 of the Code which have bearing on the decision of these cases are as under:
The policy of reservation should be made applicable only qua posts which become available after 9.10.2003
If restructuring exercise is intended to remove stagnation and improve the quality of services then implementation thereof cannot be made subject to the policy of reservation
holding: The direction given for making appointments de hors the policy of reservation cannot be termed as erroneous.
The Tribunal did not have the jurisdiction to nullify the instructions issued by the Railway Board or issue directions for making appointment by ignoring the policy of reservation.
